video.title: The Simplest $10K+/M Business You've Never Heard Of

summary: Chris Koerner interviews Rachel, who with her husband runs a restaurant specials-board ad business in Missoula and Knoxville: they give venues a free dry-erase sandwich board and sell six ad slots to local businesses at 600 USD a year each (3,600 USD per board, ~400 USD cost). They found hosts with copy-paste Instagram DMs and filled boards using guided owner referrals (12-20 names, ~6 closes). The real money is the upsell: about half of 63 advertisers bought reputation management (~400 USD/month), websites (1,000-6,000 USD) or AI receptionists via a GoHighLevel agency. They report ~50,000 USD board revenue in six months and 10,000-15,000 USD/month overall at ~85% margin; the takeaway is a cheap trusted foot-in-the-door offer feeding a higher-value service ladder.

ideas.name: Restaurant specials-board ad network
ideas.one_liner: Give busy restaurants and coffee shops a free dry-erase specials sandwich board and sell six ad slots along the bottom to local businesses for a year.
ideas.business_model: Advertising: six slots per board sold annually up front; host location gets the board free.
ideas.customer: Local service businesses (painters, HVAC, lawyers, tax, insurance, realtors) as advertisers; restaurants, coffee shops, breweries as free hosts
ideas.problem: Restaurants want a bigger, nicer specials board; local businesses want cheap, constant local visibility
ideas.offer: Aluminium dry-erase sandwich board (indoor/outdoor) with restaurant logo at top, specials area, and six printed ad spots; ad design included; board stays up 12 months under a host agreement

pricing.model: Annual ad slot, paid up front
pricing.notes: Board plus stand and markers cost about 400 USD all in (board ~350 USD incl. printing); profit ~3,200 USD for one board; nothing is printed until all slots are sold.

acquisition_channels.details: Copy-paste Instagram DMs to restaurant business pages with a photo of the board, stressing it is free; 10-20% respond; then book an in-person visit (close rate ~100% with an appointment).

quote.text: Hey, we're putting out we're looking for a local restaurant in Missoula to host one of these boards for free. Uh, you came highly recommended
quote.speaker: Rachel

acquisition_channels.details: Ask the host owner for referrals with specific prompts (insurance agent, attorney, HVAC, regular realtor customer); leave with 12-20 names, phone them, usually close about 6, filling a board in days.

quote.text: we typically leave with 12 to 20 names and then we just go call them. We can usually close six out of those
quote.speaker: Rachel

acquisition_channels.details: First board was filled in about 2 weeks with cold emails and DMs before the referral method.
Advertisers from earlier boards are offered spots on each new board; many double up.

ideas.delivery: Rachel sells hosts and advertisers; ads designed in Canva or ChatGPT image generation; a local printer prints one board at a time; she delivers the board, stand and markers and sends advertisers a photo once live; restaurant signs a one-year visibility agreement that transfers on sale.
unit_economics_claims: ~600 USD per slot, 3,600 USD per board per year
Cost ~400 USD per board all in; ~85-90% margin
~50,000 USD board revenue in 6 months, ~45,000 USD profit
63 unique advertisers, about a third on multiple boards
Host venues see roughly 7,000-10,000 customers a month; ~30 USD CPM per advertiser
ideas.startup_cost: Effectively 0 USD: boards printed only after slots are sold (~400 USD per board)
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: About 2 weeks to fill the first board

acquisition.how: Needs in-person board demos, owner referral conversations and phone sales; cold Instagram DMs to sole-trader venues are restricted under UK PECR, so software can only do the research and drafting.

onboarding.how: Contract e-sign, ad brief collection and AI ad design can be automated.

delivery.how: Printing is outsourced but boards must be physically delivered, checked and swapped.

billing.how: Annual up-front card payments via Stripe.

support.how: Advertiser updates and photo proofs can be automated; disputes about visibility need a human.

uk_applicability.notes: Restaurant A-boards and local advertising work the same in the UK. Under PECR, unsolicited marketing DMs/emails to sole traders and partnerships need consent; limited companies can be cold-emailed. Referral calls must be screened against TPS/CTPS. Pubs/cafes may need landlord/council permission for pavement A-boards outside.

risks: Not recurring until renewals: 'only as good as your last deal'
Limited number of host venues in small towns
Hard to prove ROI to performance-focused trades
Host may hide or remove the board
Cold DMs: Facebook throttles after 5-10 messages; PECR limits cold outreach in the UK

ideas.name: Board-led local marketing agency upsell
ideas.one_liner: Use the paid board relationship as a trust-building foot in the door, then upsell reputation management, websites, hosting and AI receptionists/chat widgets.
ideas.business_model: Setup fees plus monthly retainers for digital services, mainly white-labelled GoHighLevel.
ideas.customer: The same local advertisers, especially home services (HVAC, painters) for the upsell
ideas.problem: Local businesses lack review systems, citations, decent websites and miss calls
ideas.offer: Reputation management (automated review requests, review replies, posting reviews to social, chat widget), websites coded with Claude Code, hosting, AI receptionists and booking automations

pricing.notes: About 60% of digital revenue from reputation management, 30% websites/hosting, 10% AI receptionists and automations.

acquisition_channels.details: After the board is live, run a GoHighLevel prospecting report on the advertiser and email the gaps found; about half of board advertisers were upsold (20-30 closed).

quote.text: as soon as we get them paid for the board because we don't want to like overwhelm them
quote.speaker: Rachel

acquisition_channels.details: Husband posts Facebook/YouTube content about Google Business Profiles, citations and websites (800 YouTube subs, 1,300 Facebook followers); inbound DMs brought 6 customers in 3 weeks.

quote.text: he'll post content about Google business profiles, citations, websites, and he actually has a lot of people coming to him now
quote.speaker: Rachel

acquisition_channels.details: They also do a lot of cold email, testing messaging.

ideas.delivery: Rachel sells and hands off; husband builds sites in Claude Code and sets up GHL snapshots (~10 minutes per new reputation-management client plus a 20-30 minute onboarding call); monthly checks for broken links.
unit_economics_claims: Total business 10,000-15,000 USD per month at ~85% profit
Reputation management ~400 USD/month, 30 minutes one-time setup
GHL flat fee regardless of client count

acquisition.how: Upsell rides on trust from the board; reports are automated but the pitch and calls are human. Inbound content can be largely automated.

onboarding.how: GHL snapshot setup in minutes; onboarding call could be agent-led.

delivery.how: Review request flows, review replies and AI receptionists run as software once configured.

support.how: Routine fixes and questions can be agent-handled with escalation.

uk_applicability.notes: Agency services translate directly to the UK. Automated review-request texts/emails to a client's customers are marketing under PECR and need soft opt-in or consent; UK DMCC Act 2024 and CMA rules ban fake or incentivised-misleading reviews, and Google forbids review gating. AI receptionists recording calls need UK GDPR notices.

risks: Agency market crowded with cold pitches
Compliance of automated review requests (PECR, consumer law)

ideas.name: QR-code 'your ad here' board
ideas.one_liner: Place a board with six 'your ad here' QR codes in a high-traffic venue before selling any ads, since ~10% of adult visitors are business owners.
ideas.customer: Business owners who eat at the venue
ideas.offer: Board whose empty slots link to a booking/payment page

pricing.notes: Host suggestion; month-to-month with the venue, then a 12-month agreement once filled.

acquisition_channels.details: QR codes on the board itself, seen by business owners among the diners

ideas.delivery: Same printed board; landing page sells slots.
unit_economics_claims: Host estimates 700 business owners per 7,000 diners

acquisition.how: Inbound from the board itself; checkout page sells the slot.

tactics.name: Host-first, then advertisers
steps: Find a high-foot-traffic host (restaurants first, then coffee shops, gyms, breweries; avoid dentists/physio waiting rooms)
Send short copy-paste Instagram DMs with a photo, stressing it is free
Book a visit and bring the physical board; sign a 1-year visibility agreement that transfers if the venue is sold
Only then pitch advertisers, naming the venue
Print only once all six slots are paid

quote.text: you want to start by finding the host location so you can tell the advertisers where it's going to go
quote.speaker: Rachel

tactics.name: Guided referral prompts
steps: Ask 'is there anyone you don't want on the board?' with a joke
Then ask who does their insurance, who their attorney is, who they called when HVAC broke, which realtor eats there weekly
Leave with 12-20 names and phone them, naming the owner
Expect about 6 closes, filling a board in days

quote.text: who do you know or like who does your insurance? Who handles your insurance? Who's your attorney?
quote.speaker: Rachel

tactics.name: Sell reach, not ROI
steps: Ask the host for rough monthly customers
Tell advertisers they will be in front of about that many people every month
Frame it as branding: 'I see you everywhere in town'
Encourage advertisers to share photos on social

quote.text: this is truly about branding. This is about just being everywhere at a low cost
quote.speaker: Rachel

tactics.name: Micro-commitment upsell ladder
steps: Get paid for the board and place it
Email a photo of the live board
Run a GoHighLevel prospecting report; skip prospects scored at 20-30% likelihood unless they miss calls
Walk through citations and unanswered reviews; offer reputation management
Then websites, then AI chatbot/receptionist once they get more customers

quote.text: you offer them the free thing and then the $50 thing and then the $500 thing and then the $5,000 thing
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Automated review engine
steps: Connect GHL to the client's invoicing
On payment, send review requests 3 times by email and 3 by text
Reply to reviews to improve Google ranking
Post 5-star reviews to social and add a chat widget
Clone via GHL snapshot for each new client

quote.text: it's set on an automation to go out three times via email and three times via text because they're more likely to respond to a text
quote.speaker: Rachel

tactics.name: Themed boards by venue audience
steps: Pick a venue with a specific audience (e.g. Humane Society)
Sell slots to matching advertisers (vets, groomers, pet supply)
Donate part of revenue to the host cause

quote.text: we're launching two boards and from that money we're actually donating to the humane society
quote.speaker: Rachel

tactics.name: Measure host social reach with an agent
steps: Track host venues' Instagram posts showing the board
Log views to a spreadsheet
Use the extra impressions to improve close rate or prices

quote.text: anytime they post a picture of that board, you know, it could log that to a spreadsheet
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Board revenue is collected up front and is not recurring until renewals; you must keep placing new boards.

quote.text: You're only as good as your last deal
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Cold walk-ins went badly; appointments booked via DM close far better.

quote.text: walking in cold is a little bit tough, but if we have an appointment, they asked us there
quote.speaker: Rachel

warnings.warning: Facebook blocks rapid cold messages; Instagram was more permissive (and in the UK PECR restricts cold DMs to sole traders).

quote.text: Facebook you have to be careful because like it'll shut you down pretty quickly
quote.speaker: Rachel

warnings.warning: Avoid low-traffic hosts like dentist or physiotherapy waiting rooms.

quote.text: think low foot traffic places like a dentist office, maybe physical therapy where there might only be two people in the waiting room
quote.speaker: Rachel

warnings.warning: Don't open with AI; business owners are wary of it and saturated with AI pitches.

quote.text: I think a lot of them get scared when you say like, I do AI, and they're like they think it's going to mess up their business
quote.speaker: Rachel

warnings.warning: Churn is still unknown since no board has completed a year.
Episode contains promotions: GoHighLevel affiliate links and the host's Playmakers AI community.

lessons.lesson: Put ads where people already look: a specials board by the host stand gets attention without new tech.

quote.text: how do we take all of that and put it where people are already looking?
quote.speaker: Rachel

lessons.lesson: Specific referral prompts unlock names that a broad 'who do you know?' never does.

quote.text: if you ask someone something too broad, they they don't know Yes. what to say
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: A simple, familiar product is an easier first sale than AI and earns the trust needed to upsell AI later.

quote.text: offering them something so simple that they already understand and that has been around for years, is such an easier sell
quote.speaker: Rachel

lessons.lesson: Someone who has already given you money without regret trusts you far more than any cold emailer.

quote.text: It just needs needs to be someone that you already gave money to that didn't run away with it
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Collect annual payment up front when the daily cost is tiny; it removes churn and admin.

quote.text: $600 for the year is I think that's like a buck 50 a day. Okay. And that's a really easy ask
quote.speaker: Rachel

lessons.lesson: Finance/insurance/realtor advertisers buy brand awareness easily; home-service trades are harder for ads but easiest for review/website upsells.

quote.text: It's realtors, tax, insurance, lawyers. They're willing to pay 100 bucks a month, but less willing to pay 5,000 for website
quote.speaker: Rachel

lessons.lesson: Software with flat pricing (GHL snapshots) makes each extra client almost pure margin.

quote.text: If you have four customers, it costs 100, 300, 500 a month. You have 4,000 customers, it still costs 500 a month
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Local identity in outreach matters more in an AI-spam world.

quote.text: I think with the advent of AI local will be more critical more important
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Combinations of channel, industry, pricing and distribution create millions of untaken variations; 'saturated' is usually an excuse.

quote.text: 50 million ways, and 98% of them are still wide open
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Have the 'what else do you do?' answer ready so a side hustle can grow into an agency.

quote.text: these side hustles can always turn into something bigger it can turn into a really big business if you have that answer ready
quote.speaker: Rachel

evidence_quality.rationale: First-hand operator with specific prices, costs, response and close rates; only six months of history and churn unknown.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Host promotes GoHighLevel affiliate links and his Playmakers AI community; guest promotes her playbook site and agency.
